You said:
Which iPhone calendar apps let me drag appointments to reschedule them? Compare suitable options, explain limits for recurring or shared events and cite current official sources.
ChatGPT said:

If you want to press and hold an appointment on your iPhone, then drag it to a different time or day, several calendar apps support this. The important distinction is between apps that offer genuine drag-and-drop rescheduling and those that require you to open an event and edit its start time.

For most people, I'd start with Apple Calendar, Fantastical, and Calendars by Readdle. They cover different needs: a free built-in option, a feature-rich paid option, and a touch-oriented scheduling interface.

There are also two important limitations to check before choosing:

Recurring appointments: Moving one occurrence isn't necessarily the same as moving the entire series. Some apps prompt you to choose; others have restrictions on how you edit repeats.

Shared appointments: Seeing an event doesn't mean you can move it. Organizer permissions, calendar ownership, and the underlying Google, iCloud, Microsoft 365, or Exchange account can determine whether a change is allowed.

Comparison: iPhone calendar apps with drag-to-reschedule

1. Apple Calendar

Best free starting point

Built into iPhone · No additional subscription

Press and hold an event in Day or Week view, then drag it to a different time. You can also drag the handles to change its duration. Apple documents this explicitly. 
Apple Support

Limitation: The documented gesture applies to Day and Week views, not Month view.

2. Fantastical

Free basic version · Premium subscription

Press and hold events to move them in Day, Week, and Month views. Day and Week views also support resizing. It has powerful scheduling, time-zone, and calendar-management features. 
Calendar Views
+1

Limitation: Some advanced scheduling and collaboration features require Premium.

3. Calendars by Readdle

Free download · Paid features

Drag events between dates in Week and Month views, or move them to another time in Day view. Supports iCloud, Google, and Outlook calendars. 
Calendars Knowledge Base
+1

Limitation: Some features require payment; editing permissions still depend on the connected calendar.

4. Google Calendar

Free · Best for Google accounts

Google's official iPhone instructions explicitly confirm that you can drag and drop an event to a new time and date. 
Google Calendar Help

Limitation: You need editing rights; moving an event between calendars has additional organizer restrictions.

These four have explicit official documentation for the iPhone drag gesture. I would not put Outlook for iOS in the same confirmed category without stronger official evidence of direct drag-to-reschedule support.

Microsoft Support

One key distinction: Dragging an event to a new time is not the same as moving it to another calendar. The latter can involve different permissions and recurrence behavior.

Google's recurring-event editor specifically offers This event, All following events, and All events. That makes Google Calendar particularly straightforward when you regularly reschedule repeating appointments. 
Google Calendar Help

Which should you choose?

Apple Calendar: Best if you mostly move appointments within a day or week and want no extra cost.

Calendars by Readdle: Best if your priority is quickly rearranging appointments across days and weeks.

Fantastical: Best for frequent scheduling, multiple calendar accounts, and more advanced meeting management.

Google Calendar: Best if your appointments live in Google Workspace and you frequently edit recurring meetings.

My overall pick for a drag-first scheduling experience is Calendars by Readdle, with Fantastical a strong alternative if you need more advanced features.

One practical test before committing: create a disposable recurring event and a shared event in your actual calendar account. Try dragging each and check whether the app offers the expected recurrence options, saves the change, and updates other participants correctly. The official documentation establishes drag support, but doesn't establish identical behavior for every account type and shared-event configuration.
